A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same InfoSteer study. Their figures, tables, equations and research appendices can be matched reliably; v2's changed title and removal of the submission checklist do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, steering ablations, distribution-shift analyses and token-level examples in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations and analyses in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C, including the experimental results retained from v1.

M1.justification: The intervention updates, entropy regularization, SwiGLU adaptation and Appendix B steering methods remain unchanged. New Section 4.3 elaborates the surrogate characterization already described in v1 Appendix B.2, without establishing a changed steering procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same question-answering and reasoning benchmarks, GSM8K-to-arithmetic OOD evaluations, UltraFeedback instruction tuning and qualitative prompt scenarios. No evaluated dataset, domain or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same base-model and vanilla-SFT baselines and the same steering variants, including the clustering and surrogate-based variants in Appendix B.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, training budgets, preprocessing, prompts and evaluation procedures are retained. Section 6.1 newly specifies percentile regions for the existing Figure 4 analysis; this supplies previously missing detail rather than documenting a revised experiment.

E4.justification: The steering-strength ablations, task-type comparisons, OOD analysis, activation-distribution analysis, token-level cases and layerwise ablations are retained. The added surrogate explanation supplies no new ablation or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging statements and plotted error bars remain. However, removing v1's checklist item 7 also removes its explicit explanation that error bars, including those in Figure 4, indicate variation across runs. No changed run count or statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout Tables 1–8 and Figures 3–4. For example, Table 4 retains intervention scores of 66.8 ID and 86.6 OOD, and Table 8 retains 76.3 for early-plus-middle-layer intervention.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the top-K vocabulary-index set and corresponding semantic-token set in Equations 7–8. The surrogate projection, entropy-specificity reasoning and Appendix B derivations already existed; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain FFN-based knowledge-utilization steering, improved ID/OOD performance across the same model families, and interpretable token-dependent memory allocation. The revised title and abstract do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The new Section 4.3 footnote characterizes fine-grained steering as offering only marginal improvements over generic steering, explaining the paper's emphasis and identifying finer control as future work. The existing SFT-only limitation and RL/CoT discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete code-repository location, whereas v1's checklist described supplemental code. It also specifies the 0–25th, 25th–75th and 75th–100th percentile regions and expands surrogate-characterization details. Appendix A's hardware and training configuration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to model steering and FFN key-value memory research are unchanged. The added footnote equating key coefficients with Geva et al.'s memory coefficients clarifies terminology within an existing attribution.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, polishes the abstract and introduction, adds explanatory Section 4.3, expands the MLP discussion and removes the submission checklist. These are localized revisions; the scientific narrative and remaining section structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces the green-versus-blue highlighting distinction with blue highlighting and updates its caption. Added text causes page reflow, but the same figures and tables remain without substantive redesign or new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and reproducibility documentation through explicit surrogate characterization, stated percentile cutoffs and a concrete code location. Its qualification of fine-grained steering also clarifies the paper's emphasis. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of the checklist's error-bar explanation; the underlying empirical evidence remains unchanged.
